close_reason: Moot after sgrr.4 dropped the JsContactId newtype (commit 6cf54bc). No type exists to debate the redundant #[non_exhaustive] attribute on.
description:
lib.rs:60-63 declares JsContactId as

    #[non_exhaustive]
    #[derive(Debug, Clone, PartialEq, Eq, Hash, Serialize, Deserialize)]
    #[serde(transparent)]
    pub struct JsContactId(String);

The single field is private (no pub before String). Callers outside the crate
already cannot construct JsContactId(s) directly because the field is private;
they go through From<String> or From<&str>. Adding #[non_exhaustive] on top
gives… exactly nothing extra. It does forbid pattern-binding with a refutable
pattern that does not destructure: 'match id { JsContactId { .. } => ... }'
already works on a private-field tuple-struct, and 'match id { JsContactId(_)
=> ... }' is blocked by both privacy and non_exhaustive.

The maintainer cost is zero today but the readability cost is non-zero:
contributors see #[non_exhaustive] and assume there is a story about future
fields. There is not.

Fix is two characters: delete '#[non_exhaustive]'. Alternative is to keep it
but add a doc-comment saying 'Reserved for future variants such as a
TypedJsContactId(JsContactId, JsContactCardClass) shape.'

This is a P4 readability quibble more than a contract risk. Filed because the
attribute travels in the public API surface; once 1.0 ships, removing
#[non_exhaustive] is technically non-breaking but adding fields is, and the
attribute is a forever signal of intent.
title: #[non_exhaustive] on JsContactId tuple struct is redundant — field is already private
